findings.summary: A bulleted 'Depends on' line also becomes an acceptance bullet for a request that has not been read yet.
findings.evidence: `plan_entry` takes every line starting with `-`, `*` or a number as acceptance when there is no reading (reading.rs:2169, `request_text_acceptance`; doc comment at reading.rs:2111-2112). The plan accepts list markers before 'Depends on', so '- Depends on X' is both a dependency and an acceptance criterion. The behaviour is not new, but the new tests should not silently rely on it. Fix: Have the 'Depends on' tests either use an unbulleted line, or assert the acceptance list explicitly. Optionally add a note in the plan_entry doc comment that a bulleted 'Depends on' line also counts as an acceptance bullet.
findings.location: Plan decision 2 / Demonstration criterion 3(c) ('> - Depends on: B')

findings.evidence: plan.rs:345 declares `Failed(String)`. Written as in the plan, the test will not compile. Fix: Use `Ending::Failed("rejected".to_string())`, or the existing `ended(...)` helper from the plan.rs tests (plan.rs:859) if it can be reached.

findings.summary: Check that the added 'Depends on' line in the existing reading test does not change its other assertions.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:4155-4163 assert the goal (the first line), the acceptance (exactly two bullets) and the touches (exactly one path). An appended unbulleted 'Depends on 20261012-075824-1x28' line keeps all three as they are. A bulleted one would change `acceptance`. Fix: Add the 'Depends on' line unbulleted, as a separate case or after the bullets, and keep the existing goal, acceptance and touches assertions unchanged.

summary: I read the code; nothing was run. The plan fixes the fault where it starts. `reading::plan_entry` (reading.rs:2134) is the only place dependencies are built: it sets `depends_on` from `job_ids_in(text)`. No other crate calls `job_ids_in` or sets `depends_on`, and `referenced_jobs` (reading.rs:2299) needs `job_ids_in` to keep returning every id, so adding a separate `dependency_ids_in` is the right design. Keeping the retry link through `retry_reference` (reading.rs:1537) keeps the `retries` exemption in plan.rs:362 working. The plan finds both existing tests that encode the old rule: reading.rs:4164 expects 'after <id>' to be a dependency, and drain.rs:4473 queues 'This comes after {dependency}.'. A grep of crates/*/src found no code that writes 'after <id>' or 'Depends on' into a request, so nothing else relies on the old rule. The demonstrations call the real `plan_entry` and `Plan::build_with`, and each would fail without the fix. The drain integration test goes through `drain::plan` with `real_steps`, which exist today. Criterion 4 needs the records branch, which neither the producer nor the verifier snapshot has. The plan says so openly and backs it with the drain test, which is as much as can be done. The line-start rule is a sound choice, not a crude guess: it avoids matching 'depends on' in running prose, which is what the request asks for. I found three minor points and no blocker or major.
